items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I worked for Dave Grusin a lot. Dave Grusin wrote beautiful stuff for some comedy shows we used to do

ctx.x: Yeah. And that’s where the professional, again, yeah you’re absolutely right. There’s craft and there’s art as far as I’m concerned. It’s kind of like the old line, years ago someone said, “There’s music and there’s the music business.” And they’re very often two very different things. Yeah. On any given day in a Hollywood studio, and it would be the same in New York, I was sitting with the greatest players in the world, guys who

could sit in a symphony orchestra, who could do all kinds of stuff. So there was nothing demeaning or ridiculous about being there, I mean you were lucky to be there. But a lot of times the product you were going for was maybe — this, we’re not talking here Pierre Boulez, but on the other hand, in many cases it was wonderful music, great writers who took it very seriously, even if it was just fairly innocuous film, took the writing very seriously. I worked for Dave Grusin a lot. Dave Grusin wrote beautiful stuff…
You want me to pause for a second? Yes, tell him I’ll call him a little bit later. Ray Conniff is coming tomorrow.
